sections.h2: Selling a house in St. Joseph
sections.html:
Owners in St. Joseph can hire an agent, sell without one, or take an as-is bid from a cash buyer. Pick based on the condition of the house, your deadline and what the local market will pay.

Home prices here are modest. The middle value of an owned home is $154,200, so a few thousand dollars of repairs or fees takes a bigger bite out of what you keep than it would in a pricier market. Work out a net figure for every route before you decide.

  • Agent sale: wide exposure, with fees and timing set by the listing contract and the buyer's lender.
  • Owner sale: cheaper, though marketing and paperwork are yours.
  • Cash sale: the buyer accepts the house with its flaws, and the closing day is negotiable.

St. Joseph is the seat of Buchanan County, on the Missouri River about 30 miles north of Kansas City. The mid-2025 population estimate is 71,001, down 2.0% from the 2020 base. The city covers 44.04 square miles of land.

Travel to work averages 17.0 minutes, a point in favor of a house close to the center of town.

Most of the city lies in the St. Joseph School District, with Benton, Central and Lafayette high schools. A small piece belongs to the Mid-Buchanan County R-V School District. Name the right district in your listing, since families often search by it.

Shopping is concentrated along North Belt Highway on the east side, including East Hills Mall, and two interstates, I-29 and I-229, connect the city to Kansas City and Council Bluffs. The downtown portion of I-229 is slated to be replaced with a surface boulevard, so ask the city about plans if your house sits near that corridor. St. Joseph Transit runs buses in town, and the nearest airline airport is Kansas City International, about 35 miles south.

St. Joseph runs a Residential Rental Certification Program that began in July 2019 and requires rental units to pass a minimum code inspection every five years. If the house you are selling is a rental, the certification matters to a buyer who plans to keep it rented.

The city's application materials list an inspection fee of $50.00 for each inspection by a city inspector, and rentals also need a business license. Forms go to the Housing Compliance Inspection Office, 1100 Frederick Avenue, City Hall Room 107.

  • Business license for rental units: online application.
  • Unit Certification Application and Consent of Entry forms.
  • Residential Rental Unit Inspection Checklist, which shows what inspectors look for on the exterior and interior.
  • Tenant Complaint Form, useful to know about if a tenant has raised concerns.

Ask the Housing Compliance office whether your address has a current certificate before you list or sign a contract. For an owner-occupied house, call the same office to ask whether any inspection applies to your parcel before closing.

sections.h2: Recording a deed in Buchanan County
sections.html:
Deeds for St. Joseph property are recorded with the Buchanan County Recorder of Deeds at 411 Jules Street, Room 103, St. Joseph, MO 64501. The office is open Monday through Friday, from eight in the morning to half past four, and the phone is 816-271-1437. Nothing is recorded after 4:00 p.m.; papers handed in later are recorded in the order received when the next business day starts at 8:00 a.m.

The recorder cannot draw up deeds or answer legal questions and recommends retaining an attorney or title company. Call the office for current fees, because the amount depends on the document. Any recording charge will show on your settlement statement.

Roys Branch, Whitehead Creek and the Missouri River run through or beside the city. If your house is near water, gather any elevation certificate, flood insurance records and repair receipts for your buyer. Ask neighbors and the city about drainage problems before you list, so you can answer buyer questions truthfully, whether the buyer is financing or paying cash.

sections.h2: What to do before accepting an offer
sections.html:
Sort out the rental question first. If tenants live in the house, locate the lease and confirm the certification status with Housing Compliance. If you live there, ask the same office whether any inspection touches your parcel.

Then collect the deed, your mortgage payoff figure and the newest tax bill, and ask each buyer for a written offer with a closing date and a clear statement of who pays title and recording costs. A cash closing is short: you accept an offer, the title company searches for liens, you sign, and the deed is recorded at the courthouse. A financed buyer adds an appraisal and loan approval, which stretches the schedule.

Compare the offers by what each leaves you after repairs, commissions and the cost of carrying the house until closing.

faqs.q: How high are home values in St. Joseph?
faqs.a: A typical owned home is valued at $154,200 in the 2020 to 2024 estimates. Median gross rent is $898.

faqs.q: Which office handles a deed for a St. Joseph sale?
faqs.a: The Buchanan County Recorder of Deeds, 411 Jules Street, Room 103, phone 816-271-1437. Nothing is recorded after 4:00 p.m., so a late-day filing is recorded the next business day.

faqs.q: Are St. Joseph rental houses inspected?
faqs.a: Yes. Under the Residential Rental Certification Program, begun in July 2019, rental units must pass a minimum code inspection every five years, and the application lists a $50.00 fee for each city inspection.

faqs.q: Which school district covers most of St. Joseph?
faqs.a: The St. Joseph School District, with Benton, Central and Lafayette high schools. A small piece of the city is in the Mid-Buchanan County R-V district.

faqs.q: Can a St. Joseph house in rough shape be sold?
faqs.a: Yes. It can be listed, sold by the owner, or sold as-is to a cash buyer. For a rental, ask the Housing Compliance Inspection Office at City Hall about its certification status.
